title: AFTERLIGHT
satelliteSource: Cheng et al. (2026), NightNet VIIRS-like annual mean composites; HKU DataHub via faviolc Hugging Face mirror
methodology: Native 15 arc-second annual radiance averaged in aligned 16×16 cells (~7.4 km at equator). Country cells assigned by all-touched rasterization; small islands may be overstated. Radiance means and lit areas use spherical cell areas. Clusters are 8-connected cells with mean radiance ≥1 nW cm−2 sr−1 across Africa before intersection with country boundaries. Concentration = country intersection area of largest intersecting cluster / country lit area. Coverage is finite radiance area / rasterized country area; litShare is lit area / finite radiance area. Invalid native pixels are excluded from cell means. GDP is constant 2015 USD; missing observations remain null. Correlations are descriptive, not causal. Early pre-VIIRS years are model-reconstructed from DMSP observations; the source is a harmonized modelled record, not uniform direct VIIRS measurements. Sensor/model uncertainty and coarse aggregation affect cluster detection. Disputed boundaries follow Natural Earth; Western Sahara excluded from sovereign-country rankings, Somaliland combined with Somalia. PNGs reprojected to Web Mercator with one fixed logarithmic colour scale across all years.

geographicScope: All 54 sovereign African countries, including Cabo Verde, Seychelles, Mauritius/Rodrigues and South Africa’s Prince Edward/Marion islands. Country cameraBounds may frame the mainland while statistics include all country geometry. Western Sahara is context only.
